markdown_content: ## Schematic Render in CLO (2D Measurements for Tech Packs) This section explains how to open **Schematic Render** in CLO and use it to view measurements like a sketch for tech pack preparation. It also covers the key customization controls for making 2D measurements readable. Start by switching to the **Toggle** window and selecting the **Schematic Render** icon. In this view, the user can see **2D measurements** over a garment preview (initially with dark textures and dark writing). To improve visibility, the **line color** can be changed (e.g., to **white**) so measurement lines stand out more clearly. The **points of measure** can also be recolored (e.g., keeping them black or changing them to other colors such as **blue** or **purple**) to make specific measurement markers easier to see. If you want a more “sketch-like” look while keeping readability, you can use the **garment** display settings. In the **Garment** section, choose **Color** and switch the graphic appearance to **white**. You can also adjust the **brightness** to control how strong the shading/shadows appear—lower brightness reveals more shadow detail, while increasing brightness moves the look closer to white. ## Show/Hide Graphics and Adjust Measurement Visibility This section covers how to toggle graphics on/off and fine-tune brightness and color so 2D measurements remain legible on top of textures. In **3D** view, use the **Show Graphics** option (located in the **Garment Display**) to **hide or show graphics**. If the graphic is white and becomes hard to distinguish, change the graphic/overlay color to something like **gray** or a **lighter gray**. Brightness can be adjusted to help with contrast: - **Lower brightness**: reveals more shadows. - **Higher brightness**: moves the appearance closer to white. If you need to view measurements against a texture background differently, switch to **Texture** mode, and then adjust the **2D measurement colors** to improve contrast. ## Control Points of Measure via Object Browser (Points of Measure Tab) This section describes how to selectively show or hide specific measurement points using the **Points of Measure** tab controls. It emphasizes that proper naming makes the workflow much easier. In the **Object Browser**, open the **Points of Measure (POM)** tab. The interface provides **eye icons** for each point of measure, allowing you to: - **Hide** or **show** individual measurement points - Filter visibility so only the relevant markers are displayed For example, you can hide certain points and show only: - the **graphic** points you care about, or - none of the graphics and only other measurement types. This selective control helps achieve a cleaner **sketch look** and makes it faster to review exactly what you need. The video also notes that it’s easier to manage visibility when points of measure are **properly named**. ## Adjust 2D Measurement Text Size This section explains how to resize measurement text so it’s readable at any scale. Use the percentage control to make the text larger or smaller. If the measurement text is too small, adjust it using the **percent** (percentage) control to increase or decrease text size. ## Practical Workflow for a Sketch-Like Measurement View This section consolidates the main steps for configuring Schematic Render with readable 2D measurements. It combines line color, point visibility, and sketch-style appearance controls. A typical workflow is: 1. Open **Toggle → Schematic Render**. 2. Change **line color** (e.g., to **white**) for contrast. 3. Adjust **2D measurement line/point colors** (e.g., black vs. blue/purple) to improve visibility. 4. Use **Garment Display → Show Graphics** to hide/show graphics as needed. 5. Tune **Color** and **brightness** (or switch to **Texture**) so measurements remain legible. 6. In **Object Browser → POM / Points of Measure**, use eye icons to show/hide specific measurement points. 7. Resize measurement text via **percent** if needed. This setup supports quickly generating a sketch-like measurement presentation suitable for tech pack review.
